title: Talking jazz at colleges and the Penn State record machine
summary: Hodes developed a talk on jazz for colleges. At Penn State a wind-up Victrola ran down and the audience laughed, so he switched to piano.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And I developed this thing on jazz. Now, I'd done concerts at colleges. I'd been to Smith College, been to Connecticut College, I've been to any number of colleges in the East, talked on jazz.
Yeah, you've built up that circuit.
I've done that. I did it in New York.

I discovered that I could find a man and I paid for publicity. I've done all the things. New York taught me a lot. But I -- and I'd learn how to do it without records. The first time I did it at a college, it was State College, which is a Pennsylvania college.

Penn State. And in order to get there, I had to sleep in a neighboring town after working that night. I had to stay in a neighboring town, I couldn't sleep hardly at all. Catch a bus like 7:00 in the morning and be there at the school at 9:00.
And that place is in the middle of nowhere, in University Park.

And I was tired, I was in bad shape. And I got these records. I'm using records to talk about jazz, and then the piano. This is how you learn. And I put the record on, and it was a wind-me-up Victrola. It wasn't a plug-in. And I wound it up tight, at least, I thought I did. And I put on a Jelly Roll Morton record, which -- 500 boys in the room. They never heard Jelly Roll.

And it starts (singing). The record runs down, the machine runs down. And did you ever appear in front of an audience with 500 lads, you achieve laughter? They break up. Did you ever hear 500 people laughing while you're on stage, and you get red, blue, pink and azure? That's the last time I

used a record machine. They taught me very fast. I said to them, I think I better play the piano. And somebody says, I think you better. I went up and played and played and played, and when I got through, that house came down. I just played til the house came down. I just gave them my all and I just proved it.
